mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which positively impacts S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate is below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is high and unemployment is low, it indicates tight monetary policy, negatively impacting equity valuations.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high and UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary conditions, leading to lower equity returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong economic activity, leading to higher equity prices.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPI suggests potential rate hikes, negatively impacting equity markets.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 310 but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High employment with low retail sales indicates consumer weakness, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS is high and RSAFS is low but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate economic expansion, leading to higher equity prices.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.
